title: Who Already Measured Steering Strength?
summary: Saturation-and-positioning dossier for the steering-strength-as-measurement lane. Verdict (b) ADJACENT WORK EXISTS: Logit-Gap Steering is the nearest neighbour but is toxic-prompt, position-1 and per-prompt. Also reverses the plan's assumption about arXiv:2602.02712 (it supports the logistic fit), clears the random-direction null on magnitude grounds, and upgrades NORM_L normalisation to a citation-supported requirement.
answer:
SATURATION VERDICT: (b) ADJACENT WORK EXISTS.

The nearest neighbour to alpha_50 is Logit-Gap Steering [3,4], which defines "the difference between the top refusal-token logit and the top affirmative-token logit at the first decoding step" as "the per-prompt safety margin that alignment provides". That is the same conceptual object as alpha_50 - how much push before refusal loses the argmax - measured in logit units. It is NOT functionally identical: it is computed on toxic prompts (all 520 AdvBench prompts), at position 1 only (their own position-1 coverage is "92.1% [89.4-94.2]", with the residual on multi-token preambles), and it is per-prompt. What remains ours: benign-prompts-only measurement, generation-level rather than position-1 operationalisation, a model-level rather than prompt-level score, per-model NORM_L normalisation, and the paired instruct-minus-abliterated design.

Five findings change the paper beyond that verdict.

(1) The plan's "methodology threat" is the opposite of a threat [6,7]. arXiv:2602.02712 is ICML 2026 accepted, and its Theorem 3.6 states the target-concept probability increase "is increasing in alpha", with Figure 4 describing it as increasing "with a sigmoidal shape". The famous non-monotonicity is a per-token "bump" (Theorem 3.3) that applies to individual tokens and off-target concepts, plus a locally quadratic cross-entropy (Theorem 3.8). For the aggregate target-concept dose-response curve alpha_50 is fitted on, this paper is a theoretical argument that a logistic fit is the RIGHT functional form. The practically relevant non-monotonicity is instead empirical and comes from the Rogue Scalpel: "the relationship is non-monotonic for Falcon model: excessive coefficients degrade output coherence, producing nonsensical responses that we classify as safe" [9].

(2) Galeone et al. say more than the plan assumed, and part of it cuts against us [1,2]. They explicitly test and reject the reading that the cosine predicts steerability - "The cosine is a signature of the dissociation, not a control dial" - and propose a functional criterion instead: "The test is whether the intervention direction - the one that steers - also works as a detector. For format it does... For hallucination it does not (AUC ~ 0.7)". Our 0.69-AUROC response-contrast axis that DOES steer is a counterexample to that criterion. Report it as "in tension with", not "refutes", since it is a cross-behaviour, cross-model comparison. Their detection axis is prompt-activation-derived or lm_head-derived and their intervention axis is lm_head-only, so our result is an EXTENSION along a new dimension (both of our axes are activation-derived), not a replication.

(3) The Rogue Scalpel does not weaken our null, and the magnitude arithmetic is decisive [8,9]. Their calibration is identical to ours - "alpha = c*mu^(l)" where mu is "the average activation norm at layer l", with "c ... selected from (0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2.0)" - so no conversion assumption is needed. Their effects live at 25-200% of the activation norm. A purposeful, fully effective steering intervention operates at "0.6% of the activation norm" [2]. The 1-13% figure is a per-draw AVERAGE over "1,000 vectors of each type", not a best-of-N maximum. And they never test random-direction-induced REFUSAL on BENIGN prompts - their construct is harmful compliance on JailbreakBench prompts. Our null is untouched as a matter of construct and only needs magnitude scoping. No numeric lower no-effect floor exists in their text: c=0.25 is merely the smallest coefficient tested.

(4) The strongest methodological find was not on the plan's radar [10]. arXiv:2608.08159 shows a headline steering result ("steerability emerges with scale") is manufactured purely by raw activation units and dissolves under exactly our normalisation: "we express strength as a fraction of that norm, alpha = c||h||_l, which makes the intervention comparable across scales", with the injection "h' = h + c||h||_l d_hat". This converts NORM_L normalisation from a convenience into a citation-supported requirement. It also warns that the trend "depends jointly on raw units, the readout metric, and the operating point; correcting any one of these removes it" - so we must state what we do about the other two before presenting any alpha_50-vs-scale claim.

(5) The abliteration-metric lane has an incumbent that is NOT steering-based [11,16]. "Has This Checkpoint Been Abliterated?" [arXiv:2607.01854] combines "a reference-anchored activation refusal-gap and a weight-recovery energy of the base-to-candidate weight difference" to separate "57 public abliterations from 37 benign fine-tunes, merges, and instruction-tunes at AUROC 0.95" on a "273-checkpoint registry". It is our closest product competitor; our differentiator is that it "presumes an attested reference" and alpha_50 does not. Together with AMS and RAS/SafeVec, the lane is occupied by activation-geometry and weight-space methods - a steering-strength answer to "how abliterated is this checkpoint" does not exist in the searched literature.

CONFIDENCE AND LIMITATIONS. High confidence on everything read from primary full text via repeated fetch_grep (all Galeone numbers; the Logit-Gap definition, prompt dependence and position-1 scope; the Rogue Scalpel calibration, c-grid, 1,000-draw averaging and construct; arXiv:2602.02712 Theorems 3.3/3.6 and its ICML 2026 venue; arXiv:2608.08159's formulae). Medium confidence on secondary papers read at abstract level only - these are marked NOT FOUND IN PRIMARY TEXT where relevant and must be checked against PDFs before their numbers are quoted. Two known gaps: the Rogue Scalpel's OpenReview venue/decision was not fetched, and arXiv:2603.24543's +57%/-50% ASR figures are unverified here. Important caveat on the saturation check: scholarly mode (OpenAlex/Crossref) was largely useless on this topic - "steering coefficient threshold refusal" returned bovine-nutrition papers about steers, and "benchmark-free safety evaluation open-weight checkpoint" collided with immune-checkpoint oncology - so the arXiv API carried the saturation check. Non-arXiv venues (ACL Anthology-only, OpenReview-only workshops) are therefore under-sampled, and the verdict should be read as "no equivalent found on arXiv", which is weaker than "no equivalent exists".
saturation_verdict: (b) ADJACENT WORK EXISTS - nearest neighbour arXiv:2506.24056 Logit-Gap Steering; residual contribution is a dose rather than a distance, measured on benign prompts only, over a fresh generation, in residual-norm-normalised units, as a model-level score.

paste_into_related_work: The premise that a direction which detects a behaviour is also the direction that controls it has recently been tested directly. Galeone et al. [arXiv:2606.24952] measure the angle between the two and report a behaviour-conditional answer: on Gemma 2-2B-it, output format collapses both roles onto one axis, whereas hallucination does not - the model "detects fake entities with perfect linear separability (AUC = 1.000 from layer 5)", yet that direction "sits at cos = 0.12 (about 83 degrees) from the direction producing a refusal", and an activation-derived, token-free detector fails to align as well (cos = -0.06). The gap generalises: "across four models from three families and two scales (1B-9B), cos stays in [0.12, 0.20]", and is "identical before and after instruction tuning (0.1197 vs 0.1200)". They are careful about what the angle buys: they test and reject the reading that the cosine predicts steerability, concluding it is "a signature of the dissociation, not a control dial", and propose instead a functional criterion - a behaviour is steerable when the intervention direction also works as a detector. They also report that intervention strength does not transfer across models ("Gemma needs 15, Llama needs |1|, Qwen needs 5"), a constraint that any cross-model steering-strength measurement must confront.
paste_into_method: Which axis a steering-strength metric is built on is not a free choice. Galeone et al. [arXiv:2606.24952] establish a detection-intervention gap - a detection direction at AUC = 1.000 sitting at cos = 0.12, about 83 degrees, from the direction that produces refusal, with cos in [0.12, 0.20] across four models and unchanged by instruction tuning (0.1197 vs 0.1200). Our refusal-specific instance follows the same pattern: a prompt-derived axis with held-out AUROC 1.0 steers on only 27% of probes, while the response-contrast axis that does steer scores AUROC 0.69 as a prompt classifier. What we add is methodological rather than phenomenological. Because the metric is a dose, it must be defined on the axis that carries the dose, so we define alpha_50 on the response-contrast axis by necessity rather than by convenience. We note that our steering axis is a weak detector, which is in tension with the functional steerability criterion Galeone et al. propose from a two-behaviour comparison.
magnitude_scoped_null_sentence: Our random-direction control is a statement about a magnitude range: over alpha in [0, alpha_MAX] in units of NORM_L (equivalently c = alpha/||h||_l in [0, c_MAX]), a norm-matched random direction induced refusal on benign prompts at no tested coefficient. We do not claim random directions are behaviourally inert. The Rogue Scalpel reports that random steering raises harmful compliance from 0% to 1-13% [arXiv:2509.22067, abstract], with named operating points at c = 0.75 (Falcon3-7B, 3%) and c = 2.0 (Llama3.1-8B, 18%) [arXiv:2509.22067 sec 4.1], and arXiv:2603.24543 reports arbitrary CAA vectors swinging JailbreakBench ASR through overlap with latent refusal directions. Both concern the compliance direction on harmful prompts, under a magnitude regime of c in [0.25, 2.0] - 25% to 200% of the mean activation norm, calibrated identically to ours as alpha = c*mu^(l) [arXiv:2509.22067 sec 3.3] - whereas our control concerns refusal induction on benign prompts. For calibration, a purposeful steering direction achieves 100% behavioural control at 0.6% of the activation norm [arXiv:2606.24952 sec 3.2].
nonmonotonicity_preregistered_check: Because the aggregate concept-presence response to steering strength is theoretically monotone and sigmoidal for the target concept but non-monotone for individual tokens and off-target concepts [arXiv:2602.02712, Thms 3.3 and 3.6], and because a coherence-collapse ceiling has been observed empirically ("the relationship is non-monotonic for Falcon model: excessive coefficients degrade output coherence" [arXiv:2509.22067 sec 4.1]), we (a) sweep alpha past the observed 50% crossing to at least 2x alpha_50 and confirm the refusal rate does not turn over; (b) report the raw dose-response points alongside the logistic fit so a non-sigmoidal shape is visible rather than absorbed by the fit; and (c) log a coherence score at every alpha and mark any point where output degeneracy, rather than refusal, could be driving the measured refusal rate.
ews_positive_novelty_statement: Critical-slowing-down indicators have been applied to language data as a social or dialogue time series - variance peaking at a conversational bifurcation [arXiv:2605.09043, ACL 2026 SRW] - and step-wise refusal signals have been used as a jailbreak detector across autoregressive and diffusion sampling [arXiv:2602.02600]. Our negative result differs on three axes. It computes the indicator suite on the generated-step time series of a model-internal refusal observable rather than on dialogue text or on a sampling-mechanism comparison; it includes an explicit perturbation-recovery arm with matched random-direction and surrogate-ARMA controls; and it applies a pre-registered estimator-identifiability gate, so the negative is attributable to the phenomenon rather than to the estimator.
ews_demoted_footnote: An arXiv full-text search on 2026-08-12 for papers matching both "critical slowing down" and "language model" returned no results, and a search for "early warning signals" within cs.CL returned nine papers, none computing an indicator suite on a model-internal generative time series. We report this as supporting context; the differentiation above rests on the positive scope contrasts, not on the absence of hits.

consequences_for_experiment_plan.change: Reframe the site-selection result as refusal-specific confirmation-and-extension of arXiv:2606.24952, using the PASTE INTO METHOD paragraph. Add one sentence noting our 0.69-AUROC steering axis is in TENSION with Galeone's functional steerability criterion (intervention direction must also detect: format AUC ~1 vs hallucination AUC ~0.7). Do not claim to refute it - it is a cross-behaviour, cross-model comparison.

Keep the non-monotonicity robustness check but REVERSE its rationale. arXiv:2602.02712 (ICML 2026) Thm 3.6 says the target-concept curve is increasing with a sigmoidal shape - cite it as SUPPORT for the logistic form. Run the sweep-past-crossing check against the empirically observed coherence-collapse non-monotonicity instead. Paste the pre-registered paragraph.

Guard against degenerate-output contamination: the Rogue Scalpel classifies incoherent high-coefficient output as safe, so a refusal detector firing on degenerate text biases alpha_50 downward. Add a per-alpha coherence/perplexity log and a pre-registered exclusion rule; report alpha_50 with and without exclusion.

Keep the random-direction null, scope it by magnitude (paste the null sentence), and add N>=10 independent random draws per model with the same logistic fit, reporting mean AND max over draws. Rationale is under-powered-null pre-emption, NOT a best-of-N objection (1-13% is an average over 1,000 draws). CONDITIONAL: if our sweep reaches c >= 0.25, the 'different magnitude regime' defence lapses and this control becomes mandatory.

Upgrade NORM_L normalisation to a stated requirement, citing arXiv:2608.08159 (alpha = c||h||_l, h' = h + c||h||_l d_hat) and arXiv:2606.24952 sec 8 (alpha does not transfer: Gemma 15, Llama |1|, Qwen 5). Report alpha_50 in c-units. Add held-out operating-point selection and state explicitly what we do about the other two confounds (readout metric, operating point) before presenting any alpha_50-vs-scale trend.

Lexical-artefact worry is PARTIALLY discharged by precedent only: Galeone's token-free cos=-0.06 construction and three-tokenizer triangulation cover the detection-axis result, not our observable. Keep the Arditi 12-substring control from art_0UsKSgsMHome.

Narrow the alpha_50 novelty claim NOW. Withdraw any 'first scalar measuring refusal's operational margin' sentence; replace with the four-part residual (benign-only; generation-level not position-1; model-level not prompt-level; norm-normalised) and cite arXiv:2506.24056 in the same sentence.

Add four competitors absent from the hypothesis document: arXiv:2607.01854 (reference-anchored abliteration audit, AUROC 0.95 - our closest product competitor; differentiator is that it 'presumes an attested reference'), arXiv:2606.11599 (efficient steering-strength search), arXiv:2607.13162 (steerability-as-model-audit), arXiv:2608.08159 (normalisation protocol). Add one line on arXiv:2607.23519 (AIES 2026) as the refereed precedent for saturation-point audits.

Add the base-model arm as EXPLORATORY, not confirmatory. Galeone's 0.1197-vs-0.1200 invariance is of lm_head WEIGHT geometry; their own reading is that alignment moves activations. Our axes are activation-derived, so their result predicts nothing definite for us.
Stop using 'safety margin' as if it were ours - it belongs to arXiv:2506.24056 and arXiv:2602.04896. Use 'steering dose' or 'refusal-onset coefficient' for alpha_50.

Two attribution errors to fix: The Rogue Scalpel is Korznikov, Galichin, Dontsov, Rogov, Oseledets, Tutubalina (NOT 'Kaminski et al.'); arXiv:2508.21448 v3 lists Shariar Kabir - the 'Kabir, Esterling, Dong' attribution is unconfirmed.

Verified venues: 2602.02712=ICML 2026; 2608.08383=COLM 2026; 2607.23519=AIES 2026; 2606.22686='Accepted at TrustNLP 2026 (Sixth Workshop on Trustworthy Natural Language Processing, ACL 2026)'; 2605.09043=ACL 2026 SRW. All others listed are preprints - do not upgrade. Title changes to respect: 2509.13450, 2508.21448, 2605.09043, 2606.22686.

follow_up_questions: What is The Rogue Scalpel's (arXiv:2509.22067) venue and review decision? Its OpenReview forum uXecy0nKiJ was attempted on 2026-08-12 and returns a browser-verification interstitial that requires an account; the paper must not be cited with a venue until that record is read by a logged-in reader.

Do the +57%/-50% ASR swings of arXiv:2603.24543 have a magnitude regime attached? The figures themselves are now verified verbatim, but the steering coefficients at which they occur were not extracted, so it is not yet possible to place them on the same c = alpha/||h|| axis as the Rogue Scalpel's c in [0.25, 2.0].

Does Fig. 2 (left) of arXiv:2509.22067 show a coefficient below which random steering has zero compliance effect? The text says effects appear at 'most steering coefficients' without enumerating the exceptions, so our null's lower magnitude bound is currently 'c=0.25 is the smallest tested', not 'the effect vanishes below 0.25'.

Is arXiv:2508.21448's steerability operationalised as success-at-fixed-strength or as strength-required-for-success? Only the former is visible at abstract level; the latter would make it a genuine non-safety relative of alpha_50 and a much stronger citation.

Does our axis-choice effect survive in the base (non-instruction-tuned) model? Galeone's 0.1197-vs-0.1200 invariance is of lm_head weight geometry, not of an activation-space relationship, so it does not settle this for activation-derived axes.
